Provenance of the 8bpp grayscale fixtures: gray8.pcx, gray8_nopal.pcx, gray8.png

Both PCX files were produced by third-party tools, not by this package's encoder, so
they are usable as independent evidence that the decoder is right.

Why they are synthetic rather than files found in the wild:

  The PCX header has a "palette info" byte at offset 68 where 1 means color/BW and 2
  means grayscale. In practice nothing sets it to 2. Per the Encyclopedia of Graphics
  File Formats, the field "was never really used by ZSoft" and PC Paintbrush IV / IV
  Plus simply ignore it, because a grayscale image already round-trips perfectly as an
  ordinary 8bpp paletted image whose palette happens to be a gray ramp.

  This was checked against four independent encoders. Given 8-bit grayscale input,
  ffmpeg, Pillow, netpbm's ppmtopcx and ImageMagick all write 8bpp / 1 plane with a
  gray ramp in the trailing extended palette; none writes palette info 2. ffmpeg
  writes 0 there, the other three write 1.

  The one grayscale PCX that was available from a third-party archive,
  gmarbles.pcx from netghost.narod.ru/gff/sample/images/pcx/, is unusable: it is
  truncated. A strict per-row RLE decode runs out of data on row 997 of 1001, and
  decoding its whole body as one continuous RLE stream (ignoring scanline framing
  altogether) still hits EOF before filling the image. ImageMagick independently
  rejects it with "unexpected end-of-file".

How they were generated:

  # Source image: a vertical gradient for long RLE runs, plus seeded Gaussian noise
  # for literals and for bytes >= 0xc0 (the RLE run marker). 71 is odd on purpose, so
  # BytesPerLine (72) exceeds the width and the scanline padding path is exercised.
  magick -size 71x53 gradient:black-white -colorspace Gray \
      -seed 42 -attenuate 0.7 +noise Gaussian -depth 8 gray8.png

  # gray8.pcx: the real-world form. ffmpeg was chosen over the other three encoders
  # because it is the only one that pads BytesPerLine to an even number as the format
  # requires; ppmtopcx and ImageMagick both emit an odd 71 here.
  ffmpeg -i gray8.png -pix_fmt gray gray8.pcx

  # gray8_nopal.pcx: the palette-info form, which no encoder will produce. Derived
  # from gray8.pcx by removing the trailing 769-byte extended palette and setting
  # byte 68 to 2. The header and the RLE body are otherwise ffmpeg's, untouched.
  python3 -c "
  b = bytearray(open('gray8.pcx','rb').read())
  assert b[-769] == 0x0c
  b = b[:-769]
  b[68] = 2
  open('gray8_nopal.pcx','wb').write(bytes(b))"

gray8.png is the ground truth for pixel content. gray_test.go decodes both PCX files
and compares every pixel against it, so a decoding regression shows up as a pixel
mismatch rather than only as an error. ImageMagick, Pillow, netpbm and ffmpeg were all
verified to agree with it before gray8.pcx was picked.

Expected decoder behavior:

  gray8.pcx        -> *image.Paletted, 256 gray ramp entries (palette is present, so
                      the palette info byte is irrelevant)
  gray8_nopal.pcx  -> *image.Gray (no palette, palette info 2)

Removing the palette from gray8.pcx *without* setting byte 68 to 2 must stay an error
("missing extended palette"), which is what distinguishes a grayscale file from one
whose palette is simply missing.
